ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $AD$ is the angle bisector of $\triangle ABC$, and $DE \parallel AB$ intersects $AC$ at $E$. If $\frac{AE}{EC}=\frac{3}{5}$, then what is the value of $\frac{AC}{AB}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $DE\parallel AB$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ADE=\angle BAD$,\\
Since $AD$ is the bisector of $\angle A$ in $\triangle ABC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BAD=\angle EAD$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle EAD=\angle ADE$,\\
$\therefore$ $AE=DE$,\\
Since $\frac{AE}{EC}=\frac{3}{5}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{EC}{DE}=\frac{5}{3}$,\\
Since $DE\parallel AB$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle CDE\sim \triangle CBA$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{DE}{AB}=\frac{EC}{AC}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AC}{AB}=\frac{EC}{DE}=\boxed{\frac{5}{3}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right; D is located on the base BC, E is located on side AC; line segment AD is drawn from A to D, line segment DE is drawn from D to E, and the diagram and the meaning of the problem indicate that DE ∥ AB, AD is the angle bisector of ∠A. Reasoning: Because DE ∥ AB, taking AD as the transversal, we can get ∠ADE = ∠BAD. Also because AD is the angle bisector of ∠A in triangle ABC, ∠BAD = ∠EAD (E is on AC). Therefore ∠ADE = ∠EAD, two base angles in triangle ADE are equal, so AE = DE. It is known that AE/EC = 3/5, therefore EC/AE = 5/3; also AE = DE, so EC/DE = 5/3. On the other hand, from DE ∥ AB, and D is on CB, E is on CA, we can get △CDE ∼ △CBA, hence DE/AB = EC/AC. Rearranging gives AC/AB = EC/DE = 5/3. Final answer: 5/3
